title: Phishing / investment fraud - Rs 4,85,000

accused.description: Caller posed as SEBI advisor

narrative: On 03.02.2023 at about 19:42 hours complainant Kavita Deshmukh r/o Kothrud Pune received a call from a person posing as a SEBI registered investment advisor and was induced to download an app named FINSHAKTI with guaranteed returns. Between 03.02.2023 and 04.02.2023 she transferred a total of Rs 4,85,000 in four instalments to a bank account titled Green Leaf Exports, SBI Pune. When her invested amount showed as settled and she attempted withdrawal the app stopped responding. Complaint registered; IPDR and account analysis requisition issued. The credit to Green Leaf Exports was within 4 hours transferred to Nisha Traders (BoB Nashik) and then onward in small tranches to personal accounts in Pune and Delhi.

title: NDPS seizure - 2.3 kg charas, Sunil Verma arrested

accused.name: Sunil Verma
accused.description: Seized 2.3kg charas from scooter, arrested

narrative: On 08.06.2023 at about 23:45 hours patrolling staff noticed suspicious movement near Bund Garden. On search of accused Sunil Verma of Hadapsar Pune a polythene bag containing 2.3 kg charas and a mobile phone were recovered. Forensic extraction of the recovered phone revealed frequent calls to number 9009010010 and to 9987033445 in the 72 hours preceding the seizure. During interrogation the accused disclosed receiving the consignment from a courier arriving via interstate bus. Sections 8(c), 20(b)(ii)(A) and 29 of NDPS Act applied. CDR and tower data of the recovered phone procured.

title: Organized vehicle theft - 3 cars recovered, 2 accused

accused.name: Ravi Patel
accused.description: Caught driving stolen WagonR

accused.name: Santosh Yadav
accused.description: Absconding, later arrested

narrative: Between 17.08.2023 and 18.08.2023 three vehicles (Swift VDI MH-43-X-4421, WagonR MH-05-AX-9087, Eeco MH-04-Q-6633) were stolen from residential parking in Dombivli, Kalyan and Thane. A patrolling party intercepted the stolen WagonR at 03:45 hrs on NH-3; the driver identified as Ravi Patel. Two more vehicles were recovered from a garage associated with accused Deepak Khanna. Santosh Yadav was identified as the break-in operator from CCTV. Number plates of stolen vehicles were to be re-fitted on scrapped vehicles for resale. CDR of the arrested accused revealed a spike in calls among the trio in the 36 hours before the thefts.

title: Jewelry store robbery - approx Rs 22 lakh loss

accused.description: CCTV partial: 3 males in e-masks

narrative: On 14.11.2023 at about 20:05 hours three masked persons entered Manekchand Jewellers Dadar West, produced country-made pistols and decamped with gold and diamond jewellery valued at approx Rs 22 lakh. CCTV captured partial faces; suspects left on two motorcycles (one black Pulsar). Tower dump of cell sites MUM-008 and MUM-009 for 19:00-21:00 hours was requisitioned. Forensic review later matched the frame of Mohammed Ali and two persons consistent with Ravi Patel and Santosh Yadav (tied to Police Record 0932/2023 Kalyan). A number 9009010010 with no subscriber record was found logged into the same towers during the crime window.

title: Online gambling app TeenPatti Club - operator identified

accused.name: Bhaskar Rao
accused.description: App admin identified via payment rails

accused.name: Vijay Solanki
accused.description: Cash-out front-man in Delhi

narrative: IFSO Delhi traced an illegal sports-betting and card application TeenPatti Club with an estimated 2.1 lakh downloads. Financial rails showed deposits aggregating into accounts of Green Leaf Exports and Nisha Traders - the same shell accounts flagged in Cyber PS Pune FIR 0178/2023 - indicating a common controller. Payouts were re-routed through Pune accounts in the name of Priya Nair before being withdrawn. Call data of the app operator shows regular contact with Pune and Thane numbers. Sections of the Public Gambling Act and 420, 120B IPC applied. This is a Delhi-Pune linked case with a repeat-pattern money trail.

title: NDPS seizure - 620 g charas, Imran Sheikh arrested

accused.name: Imran Sheikh
accused.description: Seized 620 g charas in Yerawada

narrative: Acting on intelligence Yerawada police apprehended Imran Sheikh near Malegaon Bhau bridge with 620 g of charas. The accused has prior association with the accused Sunil Verma of FIR 0451/2023 Bund Garden. Data from his mobile shows regular coordination with number 9284033456 (Farhan Mistry, Nagpur) and brief call bursts with 9009010010 immediately preceding each consignment. On interrogation the accused stated the consignment was to be transported to Mumbai for delivery to Bhai - a description matching Mohammed Ali of Dadar. This FIR establishes the Pune supply line to Mumbai.

title: Instant-loan app fraud - 12 victims, bank insider involved

accused.name: Arun Gupta
accused.description: Ex-SBI officer facilitating account opening

accused.name: Priya Nair
accused.description: Chartered accountant, funds controller

narrative: Twelve loan-seekers in Nagpur paid processing fees to an instant-loan app totalling Rs 19,40,000 between June and July 2024. The app was reached via SMS links. Investigation revealed bank accounts were opened using KYC documents of unemployed persons, arranged through ex-bank officer Arun Gupta. The collected amounts moved to Pune accounts (Priya Nair, HDFC Viman Nagar) within 48 hours of each deposit. Accounts of Green Leaf Exports again appear in the trail. The modus operandi matches FIR 0178/2023 Pune - same shell network, different crime. Section 406 and 120B applied.

title: Arms recovery - 2 country-made pistols, Santosh Yadav arrested

accused.name: Santosh Yadav
accused.description: Arrested with 2 pistols and 11 rounds
Stored as R - handler identified

narrative: At 05:15 hrs a check-point on the Nagothane-Mangaon road stopped a motorcycle; rider Santosh Yadav was found carrying two country-made pistols and 11 live rounds. The accused has a history of organized theft (FIR 0932/2023 Kalyan). Phone examination showed a contact stored as R receiving calls after each property crime. The number 9821045451 is consistent with the network operative handling proceeds in FIRs 0178/2023 and 0234/2024. Arms were to be handed over for a planned jewelry job in Mumbai, corroborated by a call spike with 9890055667 one day prior.

title: Kidnapping plot - burner CDR ties to known network (ACTIVE CASE)

accused.description: Demanded Rs 50 lakh; victim released after 63 hours

narrative: On 10.09.2025 the complainant's son was abducted from Aundh Pune; a ransom call demanding Rs 50 lakh was received from a prepaid connection later found burnt. The victim was released unharmed after 63 hours. Tower data of the ransom device for 10-12.09.2025 shows the SIM was active only in the Pune Kothrud-Hadapsar belt. GPRS CDR of the device shows connectivity bursts at towers PUN-003 and PUN-008 co-locating with devices used by the network identified in prior Pune FIRs. The ransom number 9890919293 has no subscriber record - a burned device. This is the ACTIVE investigation against which all prior intelligence in this dataset is cross-referenced.

title: Missing woman - fake placement agency, trafficking suspected

accused.name: Sunita Wagh
accused.description: Operates 'Suraksha Manpower Solutions' placement agency, last contact with victim

narrative: On 15.03.2024 complainant Vasant Bhalerao of Man taluka, Satara reported his daughter (22) missing after she left home to join a housemaid placement arranged through an agent identified as Sunita Wagh, who runs 'Suraksha Manpower Solutions' out of an office in Khadki, Pune. The victim's phone has been switched off since 14.03.2024. Preliminary inquiry revealed the agency promised a domestic-work placement in Mumbai with an advance 'training fee' of Rs 15,000 collected from the family. Neighbours named a recruiter known locally as 'Tai' who arranges similar placements from villages in Satara and Solapur districts. CDR of Sunita Wagh's registered number shows repeated contact with a Mumbai number in the 48 hours before the victim's phone went dark. Sections 370, 370A and 120B IPC applied; women & child cell notified.

title: Trafficking transit flat raided - 5 women rescued, 2 accused held

accused.name: Iqbal Sheikh
accused.description: Operated the Kurla transit flat, arrested

accused.name: Rashid Ansari
accused.description: Found with forged passports and visa stickers

narrative: Acting on a tip generated from FIR 0312/2024 Khadki, a joint team raided a flat in Kurla, Mumbai on 25.03.2024 at 16:20 hrs and rescued five women aged 19-26, including the missing woman from Satara. Accused Iqbal Sheikh, who managed the flat as a transit point before onward 'placement', was arrested along with Rashid Ansari, found in possession of forged Emirates visa stickers and passports bearing altered photographs. Victims stated they were told they would be flown to Dubai for domestic work but had their phones and documents confiscated on arrival. Call records show Sunita Wagh of the Khadki case in regular contact with Iqbal Sheikh's number in the weeks preceding each batch's arrival. The agency's registered office was found to be a rented cabin with no valid manpower-export licence.

title: Forged passport racket linked to trafficking flat - printing set-up seized

complainant.name: State of Maharashtra (Insp. Ganesh Kore, DCB)

accused.name: Rashid Ansari
accused.description: Follow-up recovery from associate's premises: laminator, blank passport stock, visa stickers

narrative: Follow-up investigation from FIR 0288/2024 Kurla traced document supplies to a room in Kalina rented in the name of an associate of Rashid Ansari. A laminating unit, holographic overlay sheets, 40 blank passport-booklet pages and a stock of counterfeit UAE visa stickers were recovered. Devices seized show communication with a Delhi-based supplier of security paper (unidentified, number untraceable). This establishes the trafficking flat in FIR 0288/2024 was serviced by a dedicated document-forgery cell rather than an ad-hoc arrangement. Sections 420, 467, 468 and 471 IPC applied.

title: Arms interception - 6 country-made pistols recovered from truck cargo

accused.name: Irfan Qureshi
accused.description: Truck cleaner, arms concealed in false cargo floor

narrative: At 04:30 hrs on 08.05.2024 a routine check of a goods truck at the MIDC Nagpur checkpoint recovered 6 country-made pistols and 40 rounds of ammunition concealed in a false floor of the cargo bed. The truck's cleaner, identified as Irfan Qureshi, stated the consignment originated from a contact in Munger, Bihar and was destined for a buyer in Thane arranged through a Nagpur-based broker. Phone extraction shows a spike of calls between the accused and a number registered to Salman Pathan (Nagpur) in the 72 hours before interception. The truck driver was released; investigation continues into the broker network. Weapons sent for ballistic and manufacture-mark analysis.

title: 2 pistols recovered from local gang member, serial match to Nagpur seizure

accused.name: Nilesh Bhosale
accused.description: Found with 2 pistols during a routine vehicle check

narrative: On 19.05.2024 at 21:50 hrs a routine vehicle check in Vartak Nagar, Thane recovered 2 country-made pistols from accused Nilesh Bhosale, a known local enforcer. Ballistic markings on both weapons matched the batch recovered in FIR 0475/2024 MIDC Nagpur, confirming they originated from the same consignment intercepted 11 days earlier. Call records show Nilesh Bhosale in contact with Salman Pathan's number two days before this recovery, consistent with a second, smaller delivery reaching Thane despite the Nagpur interception. Investigation into broker Salman Pathan and the interstate source is ongoing.

police_station: Special Cell (Counterfeit Currency Wing), New Delhi
title: FICN seizure - Rs 9.4 lakh face value fake currency, 1 arrested

accused.name: Zakir Ali
accused.description: Held with FICN bundles in Rs 500 denomination, source handler

narrative: Delhi Special Cell's Counterfeit Currency Wing intercepted a courier on 02.10.2024 carrying fake Indian currency notes (FICN) with a face value of Rs 9.4 lakh in Rs 500 denomination, of exceptional print quality suggesting cross-border origin. The courier identified the handler as Zakir Ali, who was subsequently arrested. Phone analysis shows Zakir Ali in regular contact with a number that travels between Delhi and Pune approximately every 10-12 days, consistent with a courier run. Sections 489B and 489C IPC (counterfeiting currency notes, using as genuine) applied along with 120B IPC for the wider conspiracy.

currency: FICN Rs 9.4 lakh face value, Rs 500 denomination

title: FICN circulation - Pune shopkeeper caught passing fake notes, Rs 1.6 lakh recovered

accused.name: Dilip Ghorpade
accused.description: Attempted to deposit fake notes, cashier flagged serial repeats

narrative: On 14.10.2024 at about 12:40 hrs bank staff at a Swargate branch flagged a cash deposit by accused Dilip Ghorpade after noticing repeated serial number patterns; verification confirmed Rs 1.6 lakh in counterfeit Rs 500 notes. Dilip Ghorpade, previously known to local police for petty hawala work, stated the notes were received from a courier arriving by train from Delhi in exchange for genuine currency at a discounted rate — a pattern matching FIR 0891/2024 Special Cell Delhi where accused Zakir Ali was arrested twelve days earlier. Train ticket and CDR records place a number associated with Dilip Ghorpade's known associate in Pune Junction on the same afternoon as arrivals from Delhi on the relevant dates. Sections 489B and 489C IPC applied.

title: Builder extortion - Rs 25 lakh 'protection money' demand, threats to halt construction

accused.name: Yogesh Chavan
accused.description: Demanded protection money over phone, threatened to stall the site

accused.name: Mangesh Jadhav
accused.description: Visited site in person to reinforce the threat

narrative: Complainant Prashant Oswal, a builder executing a residential project on College Road Nashik, reported receiving repeated calls from 20.01.2025 demanding Rs 25 lakh 'protection money' failing which construction machinery would be damaged and labourers driven off site. Two days after the first call a man later identified as Mangesh Jadhav visited the site in person and repeated the threat, naming 'Bhau' (identified as Yogesh Chavan, a locally known extortion operator with prior history) as the person to be paid. Under pressure the complainant transferred a partial amount of Rs 5,00,000 on 25.01.2025 before deciding to approach police with the balance demand outstanding. CDR of the calling number shows it registered to Yogesh Chavan and frequent contact with Mangesh Jadhav in the days surrounding the site visit. Sections 384 (extortion), 506 (criminal intimidation) and 120B IPC applied.

title: Forged sale deed racket - fake ownership documents used to stake false land claims

accused.name: Suresh Patil
accused.description: Prepared forged sale deed and impersonated a notary to stake a false claim on complainant's plot

narrative: Complainant Vandana Kelkar found a forged sale deed for her family plot in Manpada, Thane registered using fabricated notary stamps, apparently prepared to support a pressure campaign to sell at undervalue. Investigation identified Suresh Patil, known locally as 'Vakil' despite having no valid legal enrolment, as the document preparer. Records tie Suresh Patil's phone to sustained contact with Yogesh Chavan and Mangesh Jadhav of the Nashik extortion case (FIR 0104/2025), and financial records show a share of extorted proceeds routed toward document-preparation 'fees' — indicating the same network uses forged paperwork to formalise land grabs once a builder or owner is pressured into selling. Sections 420, 465, 467 and 471 IPC applied.
